clue.text: The cry of a feller like Pinocchio ?

definitions.meaning: the warning shout a lumberjack gives as a felled tree comes down
the puppet boy of the story was carved from wood

explanation.surface: A man calls out the way a lying puppet might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' looks like a fellow, but it is someone who fells trees; Pinocchio, the wooden puppet in the Italian children's story, is made of the same stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodcutters shout this word as a tree falls, and the puppet's body is wood, the material the word also names.

clue.text: After your cut what next? Super !

definitions.meaning: in a card game, once one player cuts the pack

explanation.surface: Someone at the hairdresser's or card table is delighted with how things are going.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first half as card-play: after you cut the pack, the dealer's reply splits the answer into I DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect or excellent is super, the best that could be wished for.

clue.text: Expand commercially by cancelling subsidiary line?

definitions.meaning: a business that diversifies into new areas
a railway's minor offshoot line taken out of service, read as two words

explanation.surface: A firm grows by closing one of its secondary product lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the phrase literally: a branch line, put 'out' of use.
explanation.definitionFit: To diversify into new ventures is the idiom for a business widening its activities.

parts.note: Hogarth's series of paintings The Rake's Progress shows a dissolute young man going downhill

explanation.surface: An art critic describes something as increasingly in the style of the painter Hogarth.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hogarth's 1730s picture series 'A Rake's Progress' follows a debauched heir to ruin, so being like its subject is to be dissolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissolute and devil-may-care, in the manner of the pleasure-seeking libertine Hogarth painted.

parts.note: in means in fashion
an expert is a specialist

explanation.surface: A trendy consultant turns out to be clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy and lacking skill, the opposite of adept.

clue.text: Like a chess study when written down

definitions.meaning: a chess problem is printed on a board of dark and light squares
set down on paper in ink

explanation.surface: A chess problem as it looks once it has been recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess boards and pieces come in two colours, dark and light, and putting something in print fixes it in ink on paper.

clue.text: Generally it depends on nought but crosses

definitions.text: Generally it depends on nought but crosses

parts.words: Generally it depends on nought but crosses
parts.note: a general vote is decided by voters marking crosses on ballot papers, with no noughts involved

explanation.surface: Someone muses about noughts and crosses, the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generally' points to a general poll of the nation, and 'crosses' to the X each voter puts on the ballot; 'nought' pretends we are playing noughts and crosses.
explanation.definitionFit: A national vote is settled by counting the marks citizens make on ballot slips.

clue.text: The path, perforce, to Davy Jones's locker

definitions.text: The path, perforce, to Davy Jones's locker

parts.words: The path, perforce, to Davy Jones's locker
parts.note: pirates forced captives to walk along a board over the side into the sea; Davy Jones's locker is the seabed

explanation.surface: A forced route to a sailor's grave at the bottom of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Davy Jones's locker is sailors' slang for the bottom of the sea, where drowned men end up.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirate lore has victims walk along a board jutting over the ship's side and drop into the ocean.

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A nurse who has been excluded feels aggrieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like it is about the nurse being left out; it is the anagram signal on NURSE LEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling aggrieved and bitter at unfair treatment is being indignant.

parts.note: a remark is an observation or comment
able means competent, qualified

explanation.surface: A comment that is apt enough to stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extraordinary or exceptional stands out from the rest.

indicators.note: the tail of the word, its last two letters, is turned round

parts.note: apes are the primates, loosely monkeys

explanation.surface: Monkeys run away inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning tail' looks like fleeing; here it swaps the last two letters of APES, making SE of ES.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church, behind the altar.

clue.text: Replace seal back into the water

indicators.note: to replace is to place again, so these letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone returns a seal to the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replace' and 'back' read as returning a seal to the water; 'Replace' is the anagram signal for SEAL BACK.
explanation.definitionFit: An inland sea between Europe and Asia, a body of water bordered by Turkey and Ukraine.

parts.note: attractive in a way that fits a word also meaning appropriating, seizing what is not yours

explanation.surface: Someone is charming in a fitting way.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer means charming, and 'appropriately' hints that the same word also means appropriating, helping yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging and attractive, as in a winning smile.

indicators.note: two signals that the following piece appears twice

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Two social gatherings that everyone agrees were lifeless.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'dead as a ...', naming the extinct flightless bird of Mauritius.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct bird of Mauritius is the proverbial example of something no longer living.

clue.text: Do I squeal being made member of the Seraglio?

indicators.note: being made signals the letters are reworked into something new

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they will scream on joining a sultan's harem.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'being made a member'; the 'a' joins the anagram signal to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A female slave or concubine in a Turkish harem, the seraglio being the sultan's palace quarters.

clue.text: How thieves work, or stop working ?

definitions.meaning: to ... goods is slang for stealing them
to finish work for the day

explanation.surface: A question about how burglars operate, or when they clock off.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for stealing goods, and also for clocking off at the end of a shift.

definitions.meaning: Lord ..., British field marshal of the First World War

explanation.surface: Gear supplied to a cook-general, a servant who cooked and cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: A cook-general was a household servant who cooked and did general housework; split at the hyphen, the clue gives two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian kitchen range was called by this name, as was the field marshal Lord Kitchener, the British war minister.

parts.note: CR is the standard accounting abbreviation for creditor
something consumable as food is edible

explanation.surface: A lender accepts something that can be eaten, which seems believable.
explanation.definitionFit: Believable and convincing, worthy of belief.

parts.note: the cast is the company of actors in a play
an iron is the agent that presses clothes

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe's publicist is beyond criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press agent' looks like a publicist, but it is the household tool that presses clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and impossible to break or challenge, like an alibi that cannot be attacked.

definitions.meaning: to number or reckon, as in counting votes
William ..., the Swiss folk hero archer

explanation.surface: A nobleman called William.
explanation.definitionFit: Bank clerks and polling officials reckon votes or cash, and William is the Swiss archer of legend.

parts.note: a beaver is a felt hat made of beaver fur, a style long gone

explanation.surface: Someone says the beaver is behind the times.
explanation.walkthrough: The beaver here is the fur top hat of the 19th century, and the phrase means outmoded.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaver hat is old headgear, and the idiom means stale and outmoded.

clue.text: Told a story about " Softly Softly " with an edge to it

indicators.note: about signals the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to tell a story is to fib, so lied
p is piano, softly in music, so two of them give pp

explanation.surface: Someone talks about the TV police drama Softly Softly with a sharp tone.
explanation.walkthrough: Softly Softly was a BBC police drama; here each 'Softly' is P, the musical marking piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a rim or brim, as a jug has a spout or lip.

parts.note: the Greek philosopher who wrote the dialogue called The Republic

explanation.surface: A citizen of a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Republic' looks like a country; it is the title of the ancient Athenian philosopher's dialogue on the ideal state.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian philosopher, pupil of Socrates, wrote the Republic, his dialogue on justice and the ideal state.

clue.text: " There is much care and valour in this" (Hen V)

definitions.text: " There is much care and valour in this" (Hen V)

parts.words: " There is much care and valour in this" (Hen V)
parts.note: a quotation from Shakespeare's Henry V with its last word blanked, said by the king of Fluellen

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's Henry V with its final word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: King Henry says this of Fluellen, the captain from Wales; the printed clue has a dash where the word goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluellen, the captain whose care and valour the king praises, is a native of Wales.

parts.note: the way the bride walks up the church to the altar

explanation.surface: A bridle path for horses, misspelt as a wedding route.
explanation.walkthrough: A bridle path is a track for horse riders; 'Bridal' turns it into the walkway a bride takes in church.
explanation.definitionFit: The passage between pews that a bride walks to reach the altar.

clue.text: Beryl slips her marine an exotic drink

indicators.note: slips her means the gem lets go of part of herself, losing those letters

parts.note: aquamarine is a blue-green variety of the gem beryl
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Beryl slips a sailor a foreign cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: Beryl looks like a woman's name; it is the gemstone whose blue variety loses MARINE to leave the Latin word for water.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for water, a foreign word for the most basic beverage.

parts.note: bright means sunlit
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake, hence 'Scotland's' waters

explanation.surface: Liveliness found beside a sunny Scottish loch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotland's' marks the waters as Loch Ness, the Highland lake; 'by' joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Liveliness and sparkle of manner, a cheerful brilliance of spirit.

indicators.note: about signals that the poetry goes round the next word

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A poem written about a man called Paolo.
explanation.walkthrough: Paolo Veronese was a 16th-century Venetian painter, so his first name defines his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance painter of Venice, Paolo Caliari, was known by a surname taken from his native Verona.

clue.text: Figuratively speaking Cupid's is the heart

definitions.text: Figuratively speaking Cupid's is the heart

parts.words: Figuratively speaking Cupid's is the heart
parts.note: Cupid shoots his arrows at lovers' hearts, so the heart is what he aims at

explanation.surface: A remark about Cupid and the heart in poetic speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Cupid, the Roman god of love, fires arrows into hearts, so the heart is his bull's-eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The aim of an archer's arrow is the bull's-eye he shoots at.
